about: The dismissal after the last prayer following Communion. The priest greets the faithful and then, according to the kind of Mass, says “Ite, Missa est” or “Benedicámus Dómino”. In Masses for the Dead he says “Requiéscant in pace”.

about_citations.title: Missale Romanum (1962)
about_citations.locator: Ritus servandus in celebratione Missae, XI, 1

s01.narrative: After the last prayer following Communion the priest says:

s04.narrative: According to the kind of Mass, the priest says “Ite, Missa est” or “Benedicámus Dómino”. The server answers “Deo grátias”.

s05.translation: Go forth, the Mass is ended.

s07.narrative: In Masses for the Dead the priest says instead: may they rest in peace — and the answer is Amen.

w002.function: The preposition “cum” follows and joins the personal pronoun: “vobis” + “cum”.

w007.function: A plural imperative addressed to the assembly.

w008.function: A nominative noun serving as the subject of “est” (w009).

w010.function: Dative: thanks are given to God.

w011.function: Accusative plural. The verb of giving thanks is understood.
